scope: Third multiagent theoretical audit of the finite placement revision; research record outside grammatical prose.
language_facts_preserved: All published interlinear surfaces, glosses, contexts and translations unchanged in this pass.
Ordinary arguments/modifiers precede the particle field; by > och > jas > vy/so remains a partial order.
Three-stage recurrence and lower Case/concord/binding contrasts retained.
Reduced construction selection restrictions and frozen relative sources retained.

sources.supports: Tucking-in requires an explicit qualification to strict root extension; completed Case/Agree inactivity is a substantive restriction.
sources.limit: Does not establish OrdP, the Iridian placement feature or its Case-independent activity.

passages: §2, author PDF pp. 5–6: Shortest and tucking-in
sources.supports: A formal precedent for ordered multiple movement to one projection while it remains open.
sources.limit: Bulgarian wh-movement does not establish universal argument/modifier placement or the Iridian pivot-first priority. Published pagination omitted because not verified.

passages: §5.1, p. 94: pivot tucking below an external actor
sources.supports: An explicit formal alternative in which an internally merged constituent can tuck below an externally merged actor.
sources.limit: The cited analysis uses equidistance for binding; that binding account is not adopted for the Iridian ordered edge. Year checked against author publication record: 2021.

passages: §1, manuscript p. 1: remnant movement, proper binding and derivational locality
§2, manuscript pp. 2–4: differing properties of remnant constructions
sources.supports: Distinguishes derivational locality from requiring proper binding in every intermediate representation.
sources.limit: Does not independently license Iridian negative-equative movement or a general extraction-from-moved-phrase exception.

passages: §§2.2–3.1, pp. 2–5: Force, Fin, focus and Italian Int
sources.supports: An articulated left periphery distinguishes clause-edge functions, with Italian Int above Foc.
sources.limit: Does not establish the Iridian position of Pol below Foc/Ord or the order by > jas.

passages: §7, pp. 192–193: distinct A and A-bar reconstruction treatments
sources.supports: Pronunciation need not identify the interpreted occurrence, while reconstruction mechanisms vary across dependencies.
sources.limit: Does not establish uniform reconstruction or the absence of new binding/scope possibilities for Iridian Ord movement.

sources.status: existing; citation added at chain competition claim
passages: §1, author manuscript pp. 3–5: different-chain condition and case competitors
§3.1, author manuscript pp. 12–14: object shift and case
sources.supports: Dependent-case competitors exclude occurrences of the same chain.
sources.limit: Case timing is not universally invariant under displacement; the Iridian frame must retain its separately specified licensing cycle/occurrences.

passages: pp. v–vi: independent adverb/head hierarchies and their comparison
sources.supports: Comparing adverb distribution with independently motivated functional-head order.
sources.limit: Unique specifiers and a full universal hierarchy are stronger commitments than the Iridian articulated partial order; ordinary placement is not derived from this comparison.

sources.supports: Focus and question/answer alternatives; aboutness and related information-structure distinctions.
sources.limit: No §3.3.1 exists in the cited article; no claim about the syntactic position or licensing power of Pol follows from its alternative semantics.

sources.supports: A lower-copy focus-association mechanism for the studied English even construction.
sources.limit: Explicitly does not establish the same analysis for English only. The existing Iridian exclusive composition remains independently stipulated.

passages: §3.1, manuscript pp. 9–10: interaction, satisfaction and expansion
sources.supports: A comparative successive-Agree case model separating interaction from satisfaction.
sources.limit: Does not determine the Iridian participant-selection priority, phase inventory or Case timing.

repairs.finding: Case valuation previously had no explicit relationship to subsequent placement activity.
repairs.repair: Define a chain-level placement feature independent of Case/phi features, discharged only by final ordinary placement; explicitly mark departure from stronger completed-chain inactivity.

repairs.finding: The earlier account did not state its qualification to strict root extension or treatment of multiple-edge distances.
repairs.repair: Restrict tucking-in to repeated placement requirements while the head projection remains open; use ordered specifiers rather than blanket equidistance.

repairs.finding: Searching multiple copies could obscure locality and repeated registration.
repairs.repair: Search the highest accessible occurrence and register each chain once at a particular edge; phasehood remains an analytical choice rather than an inference from order.

repairs.finding: The outer CP position needed to be distinguished from the ordinary tucking requirement.
repairs.repair: Give selected finite CP status a separate outer-edge requirement applied while OrdP is open after ordinary registration; do not extract its internal arguments.

repairs.finding: Later participant movement could be misread as extracting from a displaced remnant, or as requiring proper binding at every intermediate step.
repairs.repair: Ord targets the participant at the accessible negative edge; distinguish escape, remnant and ordinary requirements and state the derivational locality interpretation.

repairs.finding: References did not by themselves derive uniform chain interpretation or invariant Case timing.
repairs.repair: Add the same-chain competitor citation and identify scope/binding restrictions as Iridian interpretation conditions; cite both Fox introduction and A/A-bar discussion.

repairs.finding: One passage conflated the clause operator with the variable; the licensing principle was overly general in wording.
repairs.repair: Distinguish Pol from the wh variable at a locally licensed lower occurrence; preserve finite/nominal domain restrictions.

repairs.finding: The shared labels could suggest an imported universal hierarchy.
repairs.repair: Explicitly distinguish the adopted Iridian Pol position from Force, Fin and Italian Int; no new particle combination is licensed.

repairs.finding: An uncited parenthetical presented head-final base order as theoretically preferable because of the same surface order.
repairs.repair: State direct complement-head linearisation as an architectural assumption, without treating surface head-finality as selecting between formal theories.

repairs.finding: The Krifka focus comparison used a nonexistent subsubsection.
repairs.repair: Correct §§3.1,3.3.1 to §§3.1,3.4; add verified Cinque preface locator.

limits: No reviewed source independently derives the whole Iridian OrdP system or establishes its phase inventory.
The selected participant priority, placement feature, edge requirements and interpretation conditions are explicitly adopted Iridian assumptions.
Richards 1997 and McGinnis 1998 original thesis downloads were inaccessible; no unverified thesis page citations were added.
Additional Poole and Keine 2024 and Rizzi/Shlonsky criterial-freezing research was considered; no further machinery was needed for this revision.
